pattern_id: Fast-path PreAcceptOK merge can create non-dense dependency ranges that deadlock execution
description: In this efficient-epaxos implementation, the leader merges dependency and sequence information from multiple PreAccept / PreAcceptOK style responses to construct the final attributes of an instance. The Exec engine (Exec.strongconnect in epaxos-exec.go) assumes that for each dependency entry deps[q] >= 0, all instances in the inclusive range [ExecedUpTo[q]+1 .. deps[q]] exist in InstanceSpace and will eventually reach COMMITTED. It busy-waits on nil entries and on instances whose Status != COMMITTED. If, due to a fast-path race or bug in mergeAttributes / handlePreAccept / handlePreAcceptOK, the leader installs a deps array that points beyond the highest actually-created instance on some replica (e.g., deps[r] = 3 while only instance 0 exists), then the executor will spin forever waiting for non-existent instances. Our test constructs a post-commit state with two conflicting commands I1 and I2 both COMMITTED on all replicas but with stretched dependency ranges (I1 depends on R1.0..3, I2 depends on R0.0..2) where only R0.0 and R1.0 exist. Executing I1 or I2 via Exec.executeCommand blocks indefinitely, violating liveness even though consensus has completed for both instances.
trigger_condition: At least two conflicting commands are proposed concurrently on different leaders, and the PreAccept/PreAcceptOK merge logic selects dependency arrays that include future instance indices without ensuring that all intermediate instances actually exist and will be committed. This can result from out-of-order PreAccept/Commit delivery, races between handlePreAccept and handleCommit, or incorrect use of mergeAttributes/allEqual when aggregating replies.
test_template:
1. Use an in-memory replica harness (like CrashReuseReplica) to build a small cluster of EPaxos replicas (N>=3) sharing the same configuration.
2. Choose two conflicting commands I1 and I2 on the same application key so execution order matters.
3. For every replica, directly populate InstanceSpace to reflect a post-race state in which:
   - I1 and I2 are both marked COMMITTED.
   - Their Seq values are plausible for fast-path commits.
   - Their Deps arrays encode dependency ranges that extend beyond the actually created instances on the other replica(s), e.g., I1.Deps[replica2]=k while only instances 0..m<k exist.
4. Do not create the intermediate instances referenced by the upper bound of the dependency ranges; only materialize the endpoints (e.g., only instance 0 exists on each log).
5. For each replica, invoke the real Exec.executeCommand for both I1 and I2 in separate goroutines while applying a bounded timeout (e.g., 500ms–5s) in the test harness.
6. Assert that for each live replica, at least one of I1 or I2 completes execution (executeCommand returns true) within the timeout. If on any replica both calls hang or time out while the instances remain COMMITTED, the assertion fails and exposes the liveness bug.
7. Optionally, instrument the test to confirm that Exec.strongconnect is spinning on nil or non-COMMITTED InstanceSpace entries in the dependency ranges, confirming the dependency-range density assumption was violated.
